meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law heritage, Samoan legislation, recognized customary land law)

Samoa–New Zealand Tax Information Exchange Agreement (2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act 2018 (Samoa); International Companies Act 1987 as amended (including the 2018 Economic Substance amendments); International Companies Regulations 2014; Central Bank of Samoa AML/CFT Rules and Guidelines; FATF Recommendations and the relevant domestic mutual evaluation framework. Beneficial ownership data is maintained in a non-public register accessible to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and the Registrar of International Companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent civil authority in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or companies authority of the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin

Certified English translation of any non-English corporate, registry, or identity documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under section 20 of the AML/CFT Act 2018 for all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories; mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and their family members or close associates; mandatory screening against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and any Samoa domestic designations published by the Financial Intelligence Unit; continuous transaction monitoring and 6-year retention of CDD records by the licensed resident agent.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: International Companies Division, Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed company names must be submitted in Latin script; non-English names must be romanized/transliterated and may require prior written consent of the Registrar; the corporate name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' as prescribed by section 16 of the International Companies Act 1987; all statutory filings and name clearance correspondence must be in English.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any name implying connection with a government, sovereign emblem, or regulated financial activity without prior ministerial or regulatory approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must file a written appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds for review and supporting evidence of entitlement to the name; the Registrar must issue a determination within 21 days of receiving the appeal; an adverse determination may be appealed to the Minister responsible for the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, with final recourse to the Supreme Court of Samoa by way of judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted. Every International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa situated at the physical premises of a licensed international financial services provider (resident agent). No virtual office or digital-only registered address is accepted for the marine towage and salvage industry, and the registered agent must be able to produce all statutory records, registers, and UBO filings for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to elevated annualized risk, estimated at 30-40%, driven by the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification of the deep-sea towage and maritime salvage sector; unannounced inspections may be conducted by the Registrar of International Companies, the Central Bank of Samoa, and the Financial Intelligence Unit, including verification of the registered agent's physical office and the company's economic substance records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 2008, Sections 4 (Incorporation), 8 (Memorandum and Articles), 18 (Registered Office), and 23 (Directors); read with the Companies Act 2001 for residual procedural matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Government of Samoa, Apia.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation as an International Company) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Company must issue at least one fully paid ordinary share (commonly US$1). No escrow or bank pre-funding account is required under the International Companies Act 2008.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Company adopts the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Registrar of International Companies; (2) the subscription of one fully paid ordinary share of US$1 by the initial subscriber is hereby ratified and entered in the Register of Members; (3) the registered office in Apia, Samoa maintained by the licensed registered agent is adopted as the Company's statutory address; (4) [Director Name] is appointed sole director and [Secretary Name] is appointed company secretary, each to serve until successor appointment; (5) the director is authorized to open bank accounts, execute towage and marine salvage operating license applications, and take all steps necessary for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed name reservation form (Form IC-10) through the MCIL Companies Registry counter or official online portal, specifying the proposed International Company name and confirming it is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name or a prohibited name under Section 6 of the International Companies Act 2008. Pay the applicable name reservation fee and retain the official reservation receipt.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and intended business description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected to or refused, file a written objection or submit an amended name reservation application within 10 business days; no additional penalty is imposed for re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed in Samoa; legal counsel authorized to practice in Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in accordance with Sections 8 to 12 of the International Companies Act 2008, including the company name, registered office clause, share capital, authorized share classes, director and secretary provisions, and indemnity clauses. The incorporator must execute the constitutional documents before a Samoan Notary Public who will verify identity and affix the notarial certificate for submission to the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Proof of physical address of incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries a constitutional clause, amend the offending clause by supplemental resolution, re-execute, and re-notarize the relevant pages for re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form IC-1 together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, the consent of the licensed registered agent, and the name reservation receipt. The application must be signed by the incorporator and verified as compliant with the International Companies Act 2008, stating the initial share subscription and the designated registered office address in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certificate of good standing of incorporator (if corporate subscriber)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected for technical non-compliance, correct the noted deficiencies and file an amended Form IC-1 within 15 business days; the original filing fee is carried forward.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Official State Incorporation Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cashier and Corporate Services Division, MCIL, Apia (electronic transfer accepted).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the official state incorporation fee of US$200 (or Samoan Tala equivalent) plus the registered agent annual fee, as per the MCIL Fee Schedule, using official government bank account transfer or over-the-counter payment. Secure an official receipt referencing the application number for attachment to the filing record.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment is not posted, present the bank confirmation or payment receipt to the MCIL Revenue Officer for reconciliation; a duplicate receipt may be issued within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review of the application and receipt of all fees, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation which evidences the legal existence of the International Company with limited liability. Verify the accuracy of the company name, incorporation date, and company number stamped on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Register of International Companies file reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, apply promptly to the Registrar for a certificate of correction under Section 16 of the International Companies Act 2008; correction is usually completed within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and licensed registered agent in Samoa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an inaugural board meeting or pass a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma First Board Resolution covering the ratification of share subscription, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of director and company secretary. The executed board resolution together with the Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents must be held at the registered office in Apia and made available for inspection by the Registrar upon request.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar notes a governance defect, pass a curative board resolution and file a notice of correction at the registered office; any late filing penalty is waived for corrections made within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Maritime and Aviation Division, Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI), Government of Samoa.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Maritime Operator Licence for Towage and Salvage (issued under the Shipping Act 1998 and Maritime Regulations), supplemented by a Samoa Ship Registry registration certificate for each tugboat and salvage support vessel.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Environmental Impact Assessment Report (full EIA) required for harbor-based salvage support facilities and wastewater discharges; vessel operation is subject to environmental registration under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL 73/78 Annex I (oil), Annex IV (sewage), Annex V (garbage), and Annex VI (air emissions); zero discharge of oily bilge water within 500 meters of Apia Harbour; wastewater discharge thresholds per the Waste Management Act 2010 and MNRE discharge consent terms; all fuels must meet local sulfur content limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the National Fire and Emergency Services Authority (NFESA) for ashore workshops and administrative premises; structural load inspection certificate for mooring bollards, slipways, and lifting equipment; occupational workplace clearance from the Labour Division of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour covering safe manning, crew competency certification (STCW), and emergency response drills.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of the Independent State of Samoa (MfR), formerly the Department of Inland Revenue — Tax Online Services (TOS) Portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) is incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 and, upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the Registered Officer or licensed Nominee applies to the Commissioner of Revenue through the Tax Online Services (TOS) portal for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) using the standard TIN application form accompanied by the Certificate of Incorporation, Registered Office Certificate, and Memorandum & Articles of Association. The MfR registers the IC as a non-resident, tax-exempt entity and may issue a Tax Exemption Certificate upon payment of the annual government fee; no separate VAGST registration is required where the IC's turnover derives exclusively from offshore towage and salvage services supplied to non-residents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), an IC may statutorily elect under section 12 to opt in to the Companies Act 2001 (becoming subject to general Samoan company law) or may apply to redomicile; no US-style check-the-box election exists under Samoan tax law, but the Income Tax Ordinance 2015 applies OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules governing offshore hybrid entities, and the IC may voluntarily register for VAGST solely to recover input tax (subject to MfR approval).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 150,000 annual taxable turnover of goods or services supplied in Samoa; an International Company supplying only offshore deep-sea towage and maritime salvage services to non-residents falls outside the territorial nexus and is not required to register.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate is imposed. Taxable persons must issue full tax invoices in the prescribed VAGST format, retain electronic records, and lodge returns via the Tax Online Services (TOS) portal on monthly or quarterly cycles; the MfR operates automated risk-based matching of ASYCUDA World customs export declarations against zero-rating claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the VAGST Act 2007 applies to: (a) goods physically exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply; (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply, including deep-sea tugboat towage and emergency maritime salvage contracts performed entirely outside Samoan territorial waters under Lloyd's Open Form or SCOPIC; and (c) supplies to holders of a valid International Company certificate where the supply is used exclusively in the offshore business. The supplier must hold contemporaneous documentary evidence of export performance and foreign-currency settlement.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Computer-Generated Sea Waybill evidencing offshore towage/salvage performance
Inward Remittance Certificate (or SWIFT/telex credited advice issued by a Samoa commercial bank) evidencing receipt of foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and VAGST Act 2007, fraudulent export zero-rating or refund claims attract a tax shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the underpaid tax, late-payment interest at 2% per month, fines of up to WST 25,000 per offence, and imprisonment of up to 7 years on conviction; refunds are retrospectively clawed back and subject to set-off where supporting export documentation is not produced within the statutory 180-day repatriation window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; the CBS administers the Exchange Control Act 1976 and Exchange Control Regulations 1977, the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended to 2020), and the Financial Intelligence Unit regime; it is the sole statutory curator of the Samoa Tala (WST).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The WST is convertible on current-account grounds for bona fide trade, service, and shipping transactions through authorised dealer banks, while capital-account transactions require individual CBS approval. Non-resident International Companies are exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976 by section 208 of the International Companies Act 1987 (unless CBS directs otherwise), so the IC may invoice, accumulate, and remit offshore towage and salvage awards (LOF 2020, SCOPIC) in USD, EUR, or AUD without conversion into Tala. Practical hurdles are: (i) authorised dealers require a CBS exemption affirmation and clean IC corporate records before crediting foreign-currency proceeds; (ii) wires entered without the s.208 exemption narrative trigger a 2-5 business day CBS compliance review; and (iii) any WST-denominated local disbursement invokes exchange-control reporting of the underlying salvage or towage service.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident export traders under the Exchange Control Regulations 1977 must collect proceeds within 6 months of shipment and surrender 100% to an authorised dealer in WST unless CBS grants a retention licence. Where the Samoa International Company (WS_IC) remains non-resident, the s.208 ICA exemption supersedes the surrender and conversion regime for ISIC 5222 proceeds; salvage awards, SCOPIC uplifts, and charter hire may be accumulated abroad and remitted offshore without conversion. The bank requires an annual CBS notification certificate, the LOF/GTCon contract trail, and audited accounts demonstrating that no Tala conversion has occurred in order to maintain the exemption architecture.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD operating account, USD escrow sub-account, and capital escrow account for injection of subscription proceeds

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific Limited - Samoa Branch (successor to Westpac Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD operating account, multi-currency accounts (AUD/NZD/EUR), and trade finance line for letters of credit
WST operational account with limited USD pass-through and capital escrow
WST-operational account only; no offshore USD/escrow architecture

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa has no fintech or electronic-money-institution licensing regime, and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended) treats unlicensed payment providers as unlawful financial institutions; foreign digital EMIs uniformly decline Samoa-IC onboarding for maritime-salvage business and no offshore Tala NDF or EMI bridge exists. The viable treasury stack remains a CBS-licensed commercial bank account for operating liquidity plus a London solicitors' Lloyds Standard Form escrow for casualty security and award settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person KYC interview is mandatory for at least one executive director and every 25%-or-more beneficial owner, or the institutional trustee's authorised officer where the IC is trust-owned; interviews occur at the bank branch or a CBS-approved correspondent office. Remote onboarding is available only through the bank's pre-approved introducer channel (typically an Australian or New Zealand commercial bank) with apostilled certified copies, live video verification, and a bank-to-bank reference; for Medium_Risk_Enhanced maritime operations the bank's compliance committee must additionally approve the enhanced monitoring plan and transaction thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value irregular lump-sum salvage awards from London arbitration (LOF/SCOPIC)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LOF 2020 salvage agreement with SCOPIC rate schedule; casualty notification and master's report; security instruments (P&I Club LOU or approved bank guarantee); arbitration award; International Salvage Union risk assessment; ISM/ISPS/SOLAS certification; audited financial statements; and a notarised source-of-funds letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indirect trust ownership with nominee shareholders and directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incumbency; trust deed and institutional trustee AML attestation; trust-register excerpt; declaration of trust; PEP/sanctions screening; CRS/FATCA self-certification; SFIU beneficial-ownership declaration filed under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Urgent casualty-driven payments to an ever-changing global counterparty set (tug subcontractors, helicopters, port agents)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Voyage/towage logs and AIS records; BIMCO Towncon/Supplytime charter; itemised invoices with full bank identifiers; registered-agent confirmation; CBS FX application where Tala conversion is sought; 2-year cash-flow projection; OFAC, UN, and Samoa FIU sanctions-clearance reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt offshore structure with non-resident directors and no visible local substance in a high-risk maritime sector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic-substance file: registered office and local secretary engagement; crew contracts and payroll; casualty dispatch records; P&I, Hull & Machinery, and FD&D insurance certificates; port-state safety inspection reports; audited accounts; and Samoan tax counsel opinion confirming the non-resident tax-exempt character.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity enters by SWIFT MT103 with narrative 'SHARE CAPITAL INJECTION - WS_IC - IC Registration No. [FILE]' and purpose code G2 (equity capital) or the authorised dealer's equivalent; the receiving bank credits the USD account without Tala conversion under the s.208 ICA exemption, supported by the directors' resolution, share-register extract, and a complete source-of-wealth file for the shareholder or shareholder trust. Lloyds Standard Form escrow settlements arrive via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 869 (other services) and narrative 'LOF/SCOPIC SALVAGE AWARD - WS_IC - casualty/vessel reference', with the final award or release instruction retained; the bank will apply a 2-5 business day compliance hold where the exemption narrative is defective, so standardised wire templates are mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements (fuel, port dues, agency fees, crew wages, subcontractor tug hire, insurance premiums) clear by SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV with itemised service invoices, routed through New York correspondent accounts for USD. Trade settlements for equipment and stores use commercial documentary credits under UCP600 and standby letters of credit under ISP98; salvage security is posted via P&I Club LOU accepted under LOF 2020. The authoritative settlement rail for awards is the Lloyds Standard Form escrow at the appointed London solicitors' client account, with release instructions requiring joint arbitrator and IC signatories; WST local disbursements require CBS Form E and conversion at the authorised dealer's buy rate, which the treasury policy should avoid for main contractual streams.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST outright forward contract with a CBS-authorised dealer, permitted only against a documented underlying towage or salvage receivable/payable and prohibited for speculative Treasury positions
USD/WST FX swap for short-term working-capital conversion of local port and agency invoices, subject to the CBS exchange-control application where the IC has elected Tala operations
Offshore WST non-deliverable forward (NDF): not permissible because the Tala is not deliverable offshore and CBS restricts NDF contracts to authorised dealers; no substitute exists

USD/AUD and USD/EUR cross-currency forward or vanilla swap to align LOF award currency with lead-shareholder functional currencies, available only where the underlying casualty contract evidences the mismatch and the bank's CBS licence permits
Natural hedge policy (primary strategy): bill revenues, fuel, insurance, and subcontractor costs all in USD, eliminating the need for hedge accounting and reducing CBS engagement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the International Company (Form AR-IC) together with payment of the annual government renewal fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after each annual anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 100 (approx. USD 35) per month or part of a month; if the annual fee remains unpaid for 6 months, the Registrar may strike the company off the international companies register and dissolve it.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register annual update and written confirmation of any share-transfer or UBO changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent on behalf of the company; maintained at the licensed registered office in Samoa and not publicly filed unless required by SIFA or a law-enforcement request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual return due date; must incorporate all shareholding transfers and UBO changes occurring in the preceding 12 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or late UBO confirmation supports AML/CFT monetary penalties against the company and the registered agent, and may be treated as a continuing cause for strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No audit is mandatory for a standard International Company, regardless of revenue, assets or shareholder count, unless the company holds a banking, insurance, or trustee licence, or the Registrar of International Companies so directs under the International Companies Act 1987.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; for a non-licensed International Company, records must reflect its financial position and may be maintained under simplified accounting acceptable to the registered agent; accounts are not required to be publicly filed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office. At each anniversary the registered agent obtains a declaration from directors and shareholders confirming that every transfer of shares in the past 12 months has been recorded, the register of directors and members is current, and the UBO particulars are accurate before approving the annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not mandatory; voluntary audit typically USD 1,500 – USD 3,500 per annum

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a licensed Samoa International Company holding a valid tax exemption certificate under the International Companies Act 1987; 27% statutory rate for ordinary Samoa-resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2015 (as amended).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Outright exemption from Samoa income tax for 20 years from the date of incorporation, extendable at the discretion of the Registrar of International Companies; exemption from dividend, interest, and royalty withholding tax; exemption from stamp duty on IC instruments; no capital gains tax; no exchange control restrictions on foreign currency accounts; annual government fee is the only recurring fiscal charge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form RIC-1) lodged with the Samoa Registrar of International Companies; exempt ICs are not required to file the domestic corporate income tax return (IRD Form 12) through the Samoa Inland Revenue Department (SIRD) electronic tax portal, but must file the RIC-1 annually and settle the annual government fee.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The RIC-1 Annual Return must be filed within three months after the annual general meeting of members, and in any event no later than 31 December of the calendar year; domestic CIT returns for ordinary companies are due within six months after the end of the fiscal year (30 June for a 31 December balance date).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered name of the International Company, registration number, registered office address in Samoa, and licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Samoan registered office and agent; the operational tugboat and salvage office abroad may be shown as a foreign business address; a Samoan service address is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part B - Share Capital and Members
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised and issued share capital, class of shares, number of issued shares, and particulars of members and beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident corporate or individual members; attach certified identity documents and proof of source of funds to satisfy the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 customer due diligence obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residential addresses, nationality, and appointment dates of all directors, alternate directors, and the corporate secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors must clearly mark their nominee capacity and provide the identity of the appointor; the natural person exercising strategic control over towage contracts must be disclosed as the ultimate directing mind.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part D - Annual Government Fee Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of the annual government fee based on the authorised or issued share capital bracket.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee must be paid in Samoan Tala (WST) through the licensed IC service provider; late payment attracts a 10% surcharge and possible late filing daily penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-certification of the IC's income-generating activity, gross income, and confirmation that Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) are performed in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify deep-sea towage and maritime salvage as 'shipping and transport support' under the International Companies (Economic Substance) regime; verify that CIGA such as strategic chartering decisions, route planning, crew management, and salvage negotiation are actually directed from Samoa and documented.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the RIC-1 incurs a fixed penalty of WST 125 plus a daily late filing surcharge of WST 25 up to a maximum of WST 1,000; continued default leads to a strike-off notice and the potential cancellation of the tax exemption certificate; for ordinary domestic companies, late CIT filing penalties are 10% of the tax assessed plus 2% monthly interest on any unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for an International Company while the tax exemption certificate is in force; the general Samoa statutory dividend withholding tax rate applicable to ordinary resident companies is 15% under the Income Tax Act 2015.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double taxation agreement relief, the foreign shareholder must deliver a current Certificate of Residence to the Samoa payer before dividend distribution; the Samoa payer applies to the SIRD for a Certificate of Residence and a Certificate of Exemption for the IC using Form IRD 21, attaching the IC charter documents, the tax exemption certificate, audited financial statements, and proof of economic substance; SIRD verifies that the IC is the beneficial owner of the income and that no treaty-shopping arrangement exists; the reduced treaty rate, where available, is then applied to cross-border dividends (commonly 5%-15% under Samoa's limited DTA network, primarily the treaties with China and New Zealand).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 15% for interest and 15% for royalties at source; IC exemption: 0% for interest and royalties paid by a tax-exempt International Company; treaty-reduced rates under applicable DTAs are typically 10% for interest and royalties; charter hire and salvage remuneration are characterised as business profits rather than royalties, protecting them from Samoan source withholding where the foreign owner has no permanent establishment in Samoa.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has not published a statutory monetary threshold for transfer pricing documentation; the Income Tax Act 2015 imposes an arm's-length standard on all cross-border related-party dealings; in practice, an International Company engaged in offshore towage and salvage should prepare and retain a Local File and Master File when annual related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000, or when related-party operating expenses exceed WST 500,000 in an exempt IC structure; contemporaneous documentation must be produced within 30 days of a SIRD request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act and associated Regulations require Samoa International Companies engaged in geographically mobile activities including shipping, towage, and maritime transport support to satisfy a Samoa economic substance test: (i) the IC must be managed and directed from Samoa, with a majority of board meetings held in Samoa; (ii) core income-generating activities such as strategic chartering, fleet deployment, salvage project approval, and risk management must occur in Samoa; (iii) the IC must maintain adequate qualified employees, physical premises, and annual operating expenditure in Samoa proportionate to its activity; and (iv) an annual Economic Substance Return must be filed with the Registrar; failure to comply results in penalties, information exchange with the OECD Inclusive Framework, and potential loss of the IC tax exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Economic Substance Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a knowingly false economic substance declaration, misrepresenting the location of vessel chartering and salvage decisions as done in Samoa while actually controlled entirely abroad, understating tug towage and salvage fee income, or backdating board minutes to conceal that the IC is a pure tax shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of up to 150% of the tax underpaid; criminal fine of up to WST 1,000,000; automatic cancellation of the 20-year tax exemption certificate; strike-off from the International Companies Register; adverse findings reported to foreign tax authorities under the Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance and bilateral Tax Information Exchange Agreements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the restitution of evaded tax and penalties; deliberate falsification attracts personal imprisonment of up to 7 years; on-exit travel bans and asset freezing orders may be imposed against directors and the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating with zero employees, no Samoan physical premises, no documented board meetings in Samoa, and using a nominee director who issues blank resignations and executes instructions from the foreign beneficial owner without independent management discretion; the IC is effectively a letterbox entity used to launder towage revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Deregistration of the IC and nullification of the tax exemption certificate with retrospective effect; imposition of a 100% penalty on undeclared income; designation as a shell company in the jurisdiction's risk rating, triggering automatic exchange of information with the ultimate shareholder's residence state; denial of treaty benefits under limitation-on-benefits clauses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face disqualification from acting as directors and substantial regulatory fines; the foreign beneficial owner is treated as a shadow director and becomes personally liable for the company's debts and tax penalties if the IC traded while insolvent or without economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions Violation in Maritime Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting salvage and towage proceeds through unreported wire channels from ships flagged or owned by sanctioned countries, structuring cash payments above WST 20,000, using an unlicensed money remitter for settlement, or failing to file suspicious transaction reports with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit despite clear red flags on the counterparty owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fine of up to WST 500,000; freezing of the IC's bank accounts; revocation of the IC registration; cancellation of the maritime towage licence; seizure and confiscation of the towage vessels under the Proceeds of Crime Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers and beneficial owners face imprisonment up to 5 years, travel bans, confiscation of personal assets, and exclusion from future maritime licensing; directors who knowingly permitted the movement of proceeds of crime are personally liable for civil restitution to the state.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper Profit Repatriation and Dividend Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends out of capital reserves rather than accumulated profits, paying unreported dividends to foreign members while declaring a nil IC return, or reclassifying excessive management fees to a related company to strip profits without commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the distribution as assessable income of the IC with a 20% penalty tax; recovery of unpaid withholding tax at 15% plus interest; penalty of WST 100 per day for each incomplete statutory record; deregistration for continued non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unremitted withholding tax and associated penalties if they authorised unlawful distributions; the Ministry of Revenue may impose travel restrictions and garnish director bank accounts to recover the shortfall.
